claims.text: The local catalog models Battle Road Summer 2002 Best in Japan second place prize as one unnumbered promotional source row containing No.2 Trainer at source index 254.
Bulbapedia says the 2002 No.2 Trainer Battle Road Summer print was awarded to second-place winners of the Battle Road Summer 2002 Best in Japan deciding tournament.
Bulbapedia's Elite Four Trainer page places the Battle Road Summer 2002 finals in Tokyo on August 17, after regional events between July 20 and August 11.

Bulbapedia's photography article says the top four ranking players of the Battle Road Summer 2002 Best in Japan tournament had their photographs featured on Trainer cards with the event logo superimposed on the image.
TCGCollector's No.2 Trainer entries preserve the Best in Japan Deciding Match second-place recognition text for Junior and Senior tournament versions, supporting the rank-specific finals lane.
Bulbapedia says the Battle Road 2002 series introduced the Master age division for players 18 and over, in addition to Junior and Senior divisions.
Bulbapedia says Battle Road Summer 2002, unlike Spring, culminated in a Best in Japan final with a new card awarded to top ranking players.

Pokumon says Junior league winners of Battle Road Summer 2002 were invited to the International Tropical Mega Battle 2002 in Hawaii, giving the Summer apparatus an international edge beyond the regional and national trophies.

No named illustrator or designer is promoted for this exact row from the attached sources; the visual-credit note is therefore kept as winner photograph / unpromoted production design rather than an artist attribution.

As judged collector texture, this No.2 Trainer matters because it makes national second place a personal image-object: the route, rank, logo, and winner photograph all have to line up before an agent treats a listing as the Best in Japan runner-up card.

Agents should preserve No.2 rank, Battle Road Summer 2002 Best in Japan finals route, source index 254, August 17 Tokyo finals context, winner-photograph construction, Battle Road Summer 2002 logo, and non-equivalence with regional No.2 Trainer, Best in Japan No.1/No.3, Elite Four Trainer, Worlds, Neo Road, or generic No.2 Trainer listings before accepting a match.

narrative.human_title: Battle Road Summer 2002 Best in Japan No.2 Trainer: the runner-up in the photograph
narrative.why_it_matters: This is the runner-up as a person, not a line in a bracket. The regional cards already showed that Pokémon cared about rank; the Best in Japan photo cards go further and put the player into the image. No.2 Trainer is where the ache of almost becomes official memory: finals route, event logo, winner photograph, and second-place text all pressed into one artifact.

steps: Confirm the rank is No.2 Trainer / second place, not No.1, No.3, or Elite Four Trainer.
Confirm the route is Battle Road Summer 2002 Best in Japan second place prize, source index 254, not a regional second-place prize.
Look for the finals context: Tokyo final on August 17, 2002 after the July-August regional circuit.
Check whether the card construction includes a winner photograph with the Battle Road Summer 2002 competition logo superimposed; this is a core identity clue, not merely decoration.

Separate this row from Battle Road Summer 2002 regional No.2 Trainer, Spring 2002 regional trophies, Best in Japan No.1/No.3, Elite Four Trainer top-four prize, Worlds No.2 Trainer, Neo Road trophy cards, Tropical Mega Battle, Secret Super Battle, Lizardon Mega Battle, and Kamex Mega Battle.
Do not promote a named illustrator unless a stronger row-level source appears; record the art lane as winner photograph / unpromoted production design.
If a seller offers winner identity, photograph, certificate, tournament paperwork, slab label, or provenance story, treat it as evidence to inspect and hash, not automatic authenticity.

Before any trade gate or spendability decision, require seller-controlled front/back images plus close-ups of title/rank, event text, photograph/logo area, surface/corners, and slab/cert/provenance evidence if claimed.
